minutes_text:
CITY OF TEMPLE CITY AND
  TEMPLE CITY UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT
  STANDING COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES

  THURSDAY, JANUARY 15, 2026

1. CALL TO ORDER

  The meeting was called to order at 4:00 p.m. at the Temple City City Hall
  Conference Room located at 9701 Las Tunas Drive, Temple City, California.

2. ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:  Board Member Georgino, Board Member Smith, Assistant
  Superintendent Wu, and Executive Assistant Montero

  Councilmember Chavez, Councilmember Man, City
  Manager Cook, Parks and Recreation Director
  Matsumoto, Public Safety Supervisor Amaya, and
  Administrative Assistant to the City Manager and City
  Council Ortiz

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 25, 2025

  Councilmember Chavez made a motion to approve the Minutes from June 26,
  2025. Seconded by Board Member Smith.

  Action:  Approved.

4 . DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. CITY AND SCHOOL DISTRICT UPDATES

  City Update

  I. E-Bikes
  • Public Safety Supervisor Amaya provided an update on e-bike
  regulations including static lighting, wattage limits, and applicable
  standards. The City Attorney is expected to present a more
  detailed overview of new legislation at an upcoming Council
  meeting.
  • City staff is working with the Sheriff’s Department to assess bike
  rack compliance at Oak Avenue Intermediate School and Temple
  City High School. As part of this effort, non-compliant bikes have
  been detained, which required parents to retrieve them from the
  school administration.
  • City staff will distribute an updated informational flyer outlining
 City Council and School District Standing Committee
January 15, 2026
Page 2 of 3

  current e-bike standards for students and parent education.
  II. Traffic Analysis Longden Elementary
  • City Manager Cook reported that the traffic engineer will provide a
  report with recommended changes to the pick-up and drop-off
  flow in the coming weeks. City staff will meet with the Longden
  Elementary Principal to discuss recommendations and
  implementation process.
  • City staff will monitor traffic patterns following implementation to
  evaluate effectiveness and determine whether additional
  adjustments are needed, including at Primrose Avenue and other
  locations as identified.

  Temple City Unified School District Update
  I. Safe Routes to School – Traffic concerns and safety issues near the
  Temple City High School
  • Assistant Superintendent Wu reported that traffic conditions at
  Temple City High School have improved, noting that City efforts
  on Lemon Avenue have contributed to these improvements.
  Enforcement actions, including issuing citations, have helped
  deter unsafe driving behaviors.
  • City Manager Cook will provide an update regarding the right-of-
  way matter on Lemon Avenue at a future meeting.
  • Assistant Superintendent Wu reported that the high school sports
  complex project is expected to be completed in February,
  including the tennis courts and softball/baseball field.

  B. DISCUSSION FOR FUTURE MEETINGS

  The topics discussed during the meeting, including e-bikes, traffic analysis
  at Longden Elementary, and safe routes to school, will be agendized for
  further discussion at the next meeting.

  Councilmember Chavez requested that the Camino Real Beautification and
  the school ballot measure be included on the next agenda.

  5.  UNFINISHED BUSINESS - None.

  6.  CLOSING COMMENTS/QUESTIONS (COMMITTEE MEMBERS) –

  Member Georgino reported that Oak Avenue Intermediate School was
  designated a National School to Watch. City and School District staff will
  coordinate recognition at a future Council meeting.

  7.  PUBLIC COMMENTS –

  Jerry Jambazian, Temple City business owner, asked about tandem riding
  regulations for e-bikes. Public Safety Supervisor Amaya provided information
  on current regulations.

  8.  SCHEDULE NEXT MEETING DATE

  The next meeting is scheduled to be held on Thursday, April 9, 2026, at 4:00
  p.m.

  9.  ADJOURNMENT

  The Meeting was adjourned at 4:37 p.m.

  Tom Chavez, Councilmember  Donna Georgino, Board Member

  William Man, Councilmember  Matt Smith, Board Member

  ATTEST:

  Bryan Cook, City Manager
